transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, mostly work stuff. I just... I keep getting up from my workstation during the day. I know I'm supposed to just stay put and, you know, finish my claim reviews, but... yeah. That's mainly what pushed me to come in.

When you get up from your desk, is it because you feel like you have too much nervous energy or anxiety that you need to work off, or is it more that you find it difficult to keep your attention on the task at hand?

I don't really think it's anxiety. It's just... hard to keep focusing. Even if I don't get up, like if I'm stuck in a long team meeting or a training, I can't really stay still. I'm usually bouncing my leg or... clicking my pen. Just shifting around in the chair a lot. I try to look like I'm focused on the presentation, but... yeah. It's just hard to sit there.
Looking back at your time in school, did you experience these same difficulties with staying focused or sitting still in class as a child?

Um... yeah, I guess so. It's not really a new thing. I remember in elementary school, my teachers would say I was smart, but... I'd always lose my worksheets. And I guess I didn't always hear the instructions. They always had to remind me to actually finish my work. So... yeah.
In your daily life, do you often find yourself interrupting others while they are speaking or finishing their sentences before they are done?
Um... no. I don't really think so. I usually just let people finish what they're saying.
Outside of your work, do you often find yourself losing things like your keys, phone, or wallet, or do you struggle with keeping your personal daily schedule organized?
Yeah, I guess so. I'm always looking for stuff I just put down... like a claim form, or my headset. Even my access badge for work. It's... yeah, it happens a lot.
When you are in social situations, like hanging out with friends or family, do you find it difficult to wait your turn in conversation or in activities?
Um... no, not really. I don't think I do that. I mostly just listen, I guess. Waiting my turn isn't really a problem for me.
Aside from the fidgeting you mentioned, would you say that you often feel driven by an internal motor or have a sense of being 'on the go' most of the time?
No... I don't really feel like that. I'm not really an 'on the go' kind of person, I guess. I just... no, I don't think so.
